text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas pledged to consider the opinion of the electorate when he nominates a candidate to the post of prime minister but said discussions on the issue will only begin after November 10 run-off elections.
- Latvia's parliament failed to pay heed to Lithuania's objections and ratified agreements with AMOCO/OPAB to probe for oil in a disputed sea-zone.

- Lithuanian National Exchange launched three indices on Thursday. Group A index will have on the list 22 companies which account for more than 30 percent of market capitalisation. Group G will follow less active companies and group VVP will track the secondary T-bill market.

- Demand for dollars in all Lithuanian banks rose sharply in the wake of Sunday's parliamentary elections in response to the Conservative party's threats to abolish the currency board and unpeg the lita from the dollar.
- Crime rate during the first nine months of 1996 rose by 10 percent compared to the same period in 1995, statistics department data show.

- A Baltic Surveys opinion poll carried out in October showed the mass media and church were trusted by 69 percent and 68 percent of respondents respectively. Lithuanians continue to view commercial banks with mistrust, with only three percent of those polled expressing trust in them.

- The leader of the Christian Democrats, Algirdas Saudargas, says his party wants a coalition on equal terms with the Conservatives. The Christian Democrats finished a distant second behind the Conservatives in the first round of the country's parliamentary elections.
- Lithuania celebrates Constitution Day today. Lithuanians approved their new constitution in a referendum four years ago.

- The temporary administrator of the troubled Innovation Bank Romualdas Visokavicius says that the bank will renew its activities in November. The rescue of the bank will cost the state 700 million litas.
